name: Synthesis Nullification — The Raw Purist Movement
creator: Originated with the writing of food theorist Adaora Petrov-Nkosi, 2207
description: Synthesis Nullification was a food culture movement that peaked between 2209 and 2216, built around the rejection of synth-protein as a valid food source and the philosophical claim that eating synthesized nutrition constituted a form of ongoing bodily colonization by corponation food-production monopolies. Its adherents — called Nullifiers or, derisively, 'rawbacks' — committed to sourcing exclusively real ingredients, a commitment that ranged from principled inconvenience for Tier 3-4 practitioners (who could afford real food at premium) to genuine hardship and occasional malnutrition for Tier 1-2 adherents who treated it as political practice. Food theorist Adaora Petrov-Nkosi's founding essay 'The Mouth as Territory' (circulated via pirate neural feed) argued that every swallow of synth-protein was an act of consent to corporate control of the human body.
cultural_impact: Synthesis Nullification produced a genuine short-term spike in demand for real ingredients on the Gray Zone gray markets, and several of its adherents became key organizers in the Real Ingredient Movement. Its more extreme Tier 1 practitioners were studied by Axiom health researchers, who published a report — widely seen as a hit piece — documenting malnutrition rates among committed Nullifiers.
controversy: The movement was deeply internally fractured by 2213 when it became clear that strict Nullification was effectively only sustainable for Tier 3-4 participants with disposable income, while its Tier 1-2 adherents suffered real health consequences. Critics called it 'luxury radicalism with a body count.' Petrov-Nkosi publicly recanted the most absolutist positions in 2214.
story_hooks: A Tier 1 community is still practicing strict Nullification in 2226, a decade after the movement's collapse — sustained by a local gray-market growing operation — and their community health outcomes are surprisingly strong, contradicting the Axiom report.

Adaora Petrov-Nkosi, now living quietly in Tier 3, is approached by a young organizer who wants to revive the movement with a modified framework; Petrov-Nkosi's response is complicated by guilt she has never publicly processed.

The Axiom malnutrition study on Nullifiers has been quietly cited in a new corponation proposal to mandate synth-protein consumption for Tier 1 recipients of public nutrition subsidies — using the movement's own casualties as justification for restriction.
